question: In the methanol-to-oil sensitivity analysis of the Aspen Plus triolein transesterification model, by how many percentage points does conversion rise from 20:1 to 30:1, and from 30:1 to 40:1?
rendered:
According to the document, at a methanol-to-oil ratio of 20:1, the conversion is 93.5%. At a methanol-to-oil ratio of 30:1, the conversion is 96.4%. 

To find the rise in conversion from 20:1 to 30:1, subtract the lower conversion from the higher conversion: 
96.4 - 93.5 = 2.9 percentage points

At a methanol-to-oil ratio of 30:1, the conversion is 96.4%. At a methanol-to-oil ratio of 40:1, the conversion is 97.5%. 

To find the rise in conversion from 30:1 to 40:1, subtract the lower conversion from the higher conversion: 
97.5 - 96.4 = 1.1 percentage points
